# Browser DOM toolkit

`#use dom` provides reusable element handles and error rams. Compile for the browser:

```sh
./edva client.dva -target wasm32-unknown-unknown -o client.wasm
```

The compiler writes the matching `client.dom.js` adapter beside the Wasm file.
Load it as an ES module, then compose the application imports with the adapter:

```js
import { instantiateDOM } from './client.dom.js';
const { instance, dom } = await instantiateDOM(
  await (await fetch('./client.wasm')).arrayBuffer(), applicationImports
);
instance.exports.main(0, 0);
// Invoke an exported application initializer after main initializes module state.
instance.exports.start();
```

The adapter supplies the C memory functions needed by the Edva runtime. An existing
loader can use `createDOMAdapter()`, merge `adapter.imports.env` into its imports,
and call `adapter.attach(instance)` before executing any Edva code.

For HTML containing `#output` and `#button`, this application resolves handles
once and captures the output handle in its callback:

```{.dva .partial}
#use dom

click: dom::Element => (dom::Event => < | Error >)
click = output => event => dom::text(output, "Clicked")

#export
   start: () => ()
   start = !=>
      output = dom::find("#output")!!
      button = dom::find("#button")!!
      writes = dom::batch!
      dom::queue_text(writes, output, "Ready") !| _
      dom::queue_attr(writes, button, "type", "button") !| _
      dom::flush(writes) !| _
      dom::close_batch(writes) !| _
      dom::on(button, "click", click(output)) !| _
```

## Properties and lifetime

Lookup with `find(selector)` or `find_in(scope, selector)` once, then reuse the
returned `Element`. Both return `<Element|Error>`; missing elements, invalid
selectors, and stale scopes have distinct error codes. `create(tag)` returns an
unattached element. `append(parent, child)` and
`insert_before(parent, child, before)` move existing nodes. `detach(element)` keeps
handles and listeners alive; `remove(element)` invalidates and releases the managed
subtree, including listeners and retained cache bytes.

The property names are overloaded statically by arity:

| Operation | Read | Write |
|---|---|---|
| Text | `text(el)` | `text(el, text)` |
| Form value | `value(el)` | `value(el, value)` |
| Checkbox | `checked(el)` | `checked(el, flag)` |
| Attribute | `attr(el, name)` | `attr(el, name, value)` |

Reads return `<Value|Error>`; `attr` returns `<<String|>|Error>`, preserving the
difference between a missing attribute and an empty value. Writes return `<|Error>`.
Use `--!` to propagate or `!| _` to abort on a write failure. Reads of unsupported
form properties return errors, matching setters.

Additional setters are `remove_attr`, `style`, `class_set`, and `hidden`.
Exact unchanged writes are tracked in Edva and can skip the JavaScript boundary.
Coupled DOM operations invalidate affected cache entries. Style shorthands require
conservative invalidation of other style entries. Form value and checked setters
always validate browser state, including silent user or script changes.

The toolkit owns managed properties. After an external mutation, explicitly call
`invalidate(el)` or `invalidate_subtree(el)` before relying on write tracking.
Handles copied from events follow the ordinary element lifetime rules.

## Explicit batches and measurements

Create a reusable `batch()`. Queue operations with `queue_text`, `queue_value`,
`queue_attr`, `queue_remove_attr`, `queue_style`, `queue_class_set`, `queue_checked`,
`queue_hidden`, `queue_append`, `queue_insert_before`, `queue_detach`, or `queue_remove`.
`flush(batch)` crosses the bridge once for the command buffer. It stops at the first
error, retains the applied prefix, and discards the unexecuted remainder.
`Error.context` contains `(failed_command_index, successful_command_count)`, both
zero based. The batch remains reusable. `discard` cancels queued writes;
`close_batch` discards and frees retained command buffers.

Live reads and immediate writes return `PENDING_WRITES` while any batch has pending
commands. No read flushes implicitly. Empty flushes stay in Edva.

`bounds(el)` and `computed_style(el, name)` read individually. For one bridge call,
create `measurements()`, register `request_bounds` / `request_style`, and call
`measure`. Retrieve by returned indices using `measured_bounds` / `measured_style`.
Failed measurements invalidate all results. `close_measurements` frees retained
buffers. Measurements are live browser queries and obey the same flush ordering.

## Events

`on(el, kind, callback)` and `delegate(root, kind, selector, callback)` accept
`Event => <|Error>` callbacks and return listener handles. `on_with` and
`delegate_with` also accept `ListenerOptions`: `capture`, `passive`, `once`,
`coalesce`, and `prevent_default`. `off(listener)` removes a registration.

Delivery is immediate by default. `coalesce` delivers only the latest event in the
next animation frame. `prevent_default` cancels synchronously at binding delivery;
passive cancellation is rejected. Cancellation and propagation requests made from
a deferred callback return an error because browser dispatch has finished.

Event data is lazy: `event_target`, `event_matched`, `event_value`, `event_key`,
and `event_pointer`. Asking for data absent from that event returns an error.
`prevent_default(event)` and `stop_propagation(event)` operate
on immediate events. Event handles expire when the callback returns, including on
failure. Copy values needed later. Callback failures reach `on_error(Error => ())`;
the default handler reports to the browser console.

## Keyed lists

Import `#use dom/list` for the `list` module. `list::new(container, key, create,
update, dispose)` requires an empty container. Callbacks have these shapes:

- `key: Item => Key`, where Key is statically Int or String.
- `create: Item => <(element: dom::Element, state: State)|Error>`.
- `update: State, Item => <|Error>`.
- `dispose: State => <|Error>`.

Use `list::sync(rows, items(..))` with an item slice. Each key is evaluated once;
duplicate keys are rejected before DOM changes. Retained rows keep their element
and state. An O(n log n) longest increasing subsequence minimizes node moves.
`list::with_revisions(rows, revision)` configures an `Item => Int` callback before
the first sync. Equal revisions skip updates; without revisions every retained
item is updated. Failed updates remain dirty and retry on the next explicit sync.
There is no rollback of previous successful mutations. A failed move pass recovers
actual child order before the next sync. `list::close` disposes rows, removes their
nodes, and clears callback references.

The list owns its children. Create callbacks must return unattached roots and must
clean up their own resources if creation fails. Keep state and callback captures in
an arena whose lifetime covers the list, following ordinary Edva ownership rules.

## Verification

Run `npm ci --prefix tools/browser_dom`, then `make dom-test`. These tests execute
compiled Wasm with jsdom under Node, including mutation batches, events, keyed
lists, and bridge-call counts. They do not measure browser layout or painting time.
`dom.stats` exposes bridge calls, commands, DOM writes, callbacks, and adapter
allocations; `dom.memoryStats()` reports adapter-managed memory.
